newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says job setback partly post-holiday blues.
newsitem.headline: Canada says job setback partly post-holiday blues.

text.p: The Canadian government viewed Friday's disappointing employment figures as due partly to post-Christmas job losses in the retail sector, Canadian government official Barry Campbell said on Friday.

"In the post-holiday season you often see a dip because of job losses in the retail sector, and that's reflected in those numbers," Campbell, parliamentary secretary to Finance Minister Paul Martin, told reporters.
"But the overall trend has been upward in job growth the last four months -- very positive job growth figures."
He added: "There are going to be setbacks like this from time to time. It's important to look at the overall trend, which is upward."
Campbell repeated the government's position that lower interest rates resulting from the government's attack on its fiscal deficit would translate into robust growth.
